hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Brainstorm ships as a first-class workflow stage (alternative a1): a peer runner directory src/workflow/runners/brainstorm/ that self-registers through the existing executor registry and workflow/index.ts registerWorkflowRunners; a new persisted SpecArtifact peer file in src/workflow/artifacts/ with a specArtifactPaths peer in storage.ts (hash-addressed, listed, approval-stamped identically to DEF/HLD/LLD/PLAN); and an additive elicitation phase on the existing insrc_workflow_step MCP surface that reuses state-store.ts and the questions-gate primitive and preserves the opaque state token verbatim. The single cross-cutting SpecArtifact shape (intent, scope boundary, non-goals, decisions-with-ruled-out-alternatives, open items) is read unchanged by both define (s8) and standalone design.story (s9). Nothing touches the shared/chat-agent brainstorm.addIdea stub.

ownedContracts.name: SpecArtifact record + hash-addressed persistence
ownedContracts.purpose: The one durable, structured spec both downstream stages read. A typed record (like define.ts/plan.ts) persisted hash-addressed with approval stamping via a storage.ts peer, so it is listed and approval-gated identically to every other workflow artifact and no consumer-specific variant exists (k1,k6,k7).

boundary.internal: The concrete SpecArtifact serialization + markdown rendering and the specArtifactPaths hash-addressing + atomic write, plus how the spec is surfaced in the existing artifact listing. The field set is the sc1 contract; the on-disk format details and renderer are internal to s6.

hldContextSlice.rolloutPhase: Phase C — Persist + review/approve the spec

nonFunctional.performance: Elicitation is interactive and controller-paced; there is no daemon-side latency SLA because the daemon runs no autonomous loop (k2). The stage sits on the critical design path and uses the core model tier — correctness of the elicited spec is never traded for fewer or cheaper model calls (k13).
nonFunctional.security: No new external surface. The MCP layer never opens LMDB/LanceDB; the SpecArtifact is read/written only through daemon IPC (k11). The stage is namespaced distinctly from the shared/chat-agent brainstorm.addIdea offlineRpc stub and never invokes it (k10).
nonFunctional.observability: The stage emits the same step-start/step-done/synthesize progress frames as the existing stages, and the SpecArtifact appears in the same artifact listing surfaces, so an in-flight or completed brainstorm is observable exactly like any other stage (ac3).
nonFunctional.durability: The SpecArtifact is hash-addressed and written atomically via the existing storage writeAtomic path; reading it back returns identical content. Approval is a durable meta.approvedAt stamp; an abandoned conversation persists nothing (s3/ac5), and an unapproved spec cannot be consumed (k12).

api.name: SpecArtifact

returns.meaning: The durable, structured spec record both downstream stages read (sc1). Declared in a new src/workflow/artifacts/spec.ts peer of define.ts/plan.ts, using the shared WorkflowArtifact<Body> envelope + ArtifactMetaBase (createdAt, optional approvedAt/review + model attribution). category reuses the REAL BrainstormCategory union; SpecDecision uses `chosen` (matching the s4 elicit field).

preconditions: Constructed only from a confirmed converged elicit output (s3/s4).
postconditions: kind is 'spec'; meta.approvedAt is unset at creation (set only by s7's approve gate, k12).

parameters.purpose: The record to render to the human-facing markdown.

Not a transcript (ac2). Peer of define.ts's renderer.

postconditions: Contains the artifactId marker and one section per SpecArtifactBody field.

parameters.name: specHash
parameters.purpose: The deterministic hash id of the converged spec.

errorCases.scenario: The brainstormSynthesizer emits a body missing a required SpecArtifactBody field (e.g. no scopeBoundary), or a decisions entry missing chosen/ruledOut/reason.
errorCases.detection: finalizeBrainstorm validates the synthesized body against the SpecArtifactBody shape (the same validate-before-write discipline finalizeDefine/finalizePlan use) before constructing the SpecArtifact.
errorCases.response: finalize returns a retryable error and writes NOTHING (validation precedes writeAtomic); the synth turn is re-issued rather than persisting a partial spec.
errorCases.userImpact: No half-formed spec ever lands on disk; the run either produces a complete structured spec or none.

errorCases.scenario: The synthesizer collapses the whole request into intent and leaves scopeBoundary empty (or vice-versa) — an under-structured statement that would read like a transcript.
errorCases.detection: renderSpecMarkdown + the shape validation require both intent and scopeBoundary to be non-empty strings; an empty scopeBoundary fails validation before persistence.
errorCases.response: Rejected as a validation error (retryable); the synthesizer prompt requires the converged statement be split into distinct intent + scope boundary.
errorCases.userImpact: The recorded spec always reads as a structured statement (ac2), not a single blob.

errorCases.scenario: A writeAtomic partial-failure (e.g. the md write succeeds but the json write is interrupted), risking a spec listed without its canonical record or vice-versa.
errorCases.detection: writeAtomic writes to <path>.tmp then renames; finalize writes json + md through it and surfaces any thrown fs error. A crash between the two leaves at most a completed file and a stale .tmp, never a torn file.
errorCases.response: The fs error propagates out of finalize (the run errors); because each file is written tmp-then-rename, no partially-written artifact is readable, and re-running finalize with the same specHash overwrites idempotently.
errorCases.userImpact: A reader never sees a torn spec; at worst the run is retried and the same hash-addressed pair is rewritten.

errorCases.scenario: finalizeBrainstorm is reached but the run never actually confirmed (a caller drives synthesize on an unconfirmed elicit output).
errorCases.detection: The converged elicit output carries confirmed:true only after the s3 gate; the synthesizer input is the finalized step output, which the executor only advances past on a confirmed resume. An unconfirmed output would not have reached synthesize.
errorCases.response: Structurally unreachable via the normal executor path; if forced, the missing/short converged fields fail the same body validation.
errorCases.userImpact: Only a user-confirmed converged statement is ever persisted as a spec (k12 lineage; abandonment persists nothing).

edgeCases.input: A fork-free convergence: decisions:[] and nonGoals:[] (the user's idea had a single obvious scope).
edgeCases.expected: A valid SpecArtifact with empty decisions/nonGoals arrays; renderSpecMarkdown emits the sections as empty (e.g. '_none_'), still a complete structured spec (ac2).

edgeCases.input: Two different converged specs produced in the same repo (two brainstorm runs).
edgeCases.expected: Each gets its own specHash -> distinct SPEC-<hash>.json under ARTIFACTS_DIR + md under SPECS_DIR; both are listed alongside the other artifacts, neither overwrites the other (ac1/ac3).

edgeCases.input: The identical converged body is finalized twice (deterministic content).
edgeCases.expected: specHash is deterministic over the body, so the same SPEC-<hash> pair is produced and writeAtomic overwrites idempotently — reading back returns identical content (ac1).

edgeCases.input: openItems is non-empty on the confirmed spec (the user confirmed intent but left some questions open).
edgeCases.expected: The open items are recorded in the SpecArtifactBody.openItems section — a valid spec (a confirmed statement may still carry open items; that is orthogonal to convergence).

alternativesConsidered.name: Peer SpecArtifact record + storage peer, structured body, wired through the brainstorm synthesize/finalize seam
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: A new src/workflow/artifacts/spec.ts (record + renderer) + storage.ts peers (SPECS_DIR/specArtifactId/specArtifactPaths/specMdRel) mirroring define/plan; the brainstorm synthesizer structures the converged elicit output into the single SpecArtifactBody { intent, scopeBoundary, nonGoals, decisions, openItems } and finalize persists it hash-addressed via writeAtomic.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Realize sc1 exactly as the HLD prescribes. (1) src/workflow/artifacts/spec.ts declares SpecArtifactBody { category, intent, scopeBoundary, nonGoals, decisions:[{chosen,ruledOut,reason}], openItems }, SpecArtifact = WorkflowArtifact<SpecArtifactBody> with kind 'spec' + specHash + meta (createdAt, optional approvedAt/review/model), and renderSpecMarkdown emitting the structured sections + artifactIdMarker (peer of define.ts/plan.ts). (2) storage.ts gains SPECS_DIR, specArtifactId(specHash), specArtifactPaths(repoPath, specHash) -> { md under SPECS_DIR, json under ARTIFACTS_DIR }, specMdRel. (3) orchestrator.ts: a brainstormSynthesizer (prepareSynthesize case) prompts the LLM to STRUCTURE the converged workingStatement into distinct intent + scopeBoundary and carry decisions/nonGoals/openItems 1:1; finalizeBrainstorm (finalizeArtifact case) validates, computes specHash, writes {md,json} via specArtifactPaths+writeAtomic, stamps meta.createdAt + attribution, leaving approvedAt unset (s7's gate). The 'not yet supported' brainstorm arms are removed. ONE artifact, no consumer variant; listed + approval-gated exactly like DEF/HLD/LLD/PLAN. Category reuses the REAL BrainstormCategory union (recorded refinement).
pros: Directly implements sc1 + k1/k6/k7: one cross-cutting SpecArtifact, listed/approval-stamped identically to every other artifact via the existing ARTIFACTS_DIR + writeAtomic path (ac1/ac3/ac4).

ac2 is structural: the synthesizer splits the converged statement into typed intent + scopeBoundary + non-goals + decisions + open-items, so the record reads as a statement of the request, not a transcript.
Reuses the proven define/plan artifact+storage+finalize template end-to-end — no new subsystem, no new persistence path; MCP never touches LMDB/Lance (k11).
Completes the brainstorm workflow: prepareSynthesize/finalizeArtifact stop throwing, so a brainstorm run now yields an approvable artifact.
cons: Largest of the three (new artifact file + storage peers + orchestrator wiring + tests) — but that IS sc1's scope; size M.
The intent/scopeBoundary split is synthesizer-prompt-governed (LLM structures the converged statement) — acceptable on the core tier (k13).

alternativesConsidered.name: Persist the raw converged elicit output verbatim as the artifact body
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Store the s3/s4 elicit output shape { category, workingStatement, openItems, confirmed, decisions, nonGoals } directly as the SpecArtifact body, skipping the intent/scopeBoundary structuring.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add the spec.ts record + storage peers, but set SpecArtifactBody = the elicit output as-is (a single workingStatement blob + decisions/nonGoals/openItems), and have finalize persist that without a synthesizer restructuring step.
pros: Smaller — no synthesizer prompt; the converged output is written straight through.
Still a peer artifact, hash-addressed + listed (ac1/ac3 hold).
cons: Violates ac2/k1: the sc1 body is { intent, scopeBoundary, ... } — a single workingStatement blob is a mid-conversation artifact, not the structured statement (intent vs scope boundary distinct) the story requires; it reads closer to a transcript snapshot.

Pushes structuring onto every downstream consumer (define s8, design.story s9), which must each re-parse the blob — breaking 'one shape read unchanged by both' and inviting consumer-specific interpretation (ac4 risk).
Leaks the internal elicit continuation shape (confirmed flag, working memory) into the durable public artifact.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Under-structures the body: a single workingStatement blob is not the { intent, scopeBoundary, ... } structured statement ac2/k1 require (ac2 violates), and it forces each downstream consumer to re-parse the blob, inviting a consumer-specific variant (ac4 partial). Ranked 2nd.

alternativesConsidered.name: A bespoke spec store / on-disk format separate from the artifact module
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Persist the spec in its own dedicated store or format (not a peer artifact file), with a bespoke lookup rather than the shared artifact listing.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Introduce a spec-specific persistence path (e.g. a separate directory + index) and a dedicated read/list API for the spec, outside the define/plan artifact+storage template.
pros: Could tailor the spec's on-disk layout independently of the other artifacts.
cons: Violates k6/k7/ac3: the spec would NOT be found through the same listing/lookup as the other workflow artifacts — a separate place to go looking, the exact failure ac3 forbids.
Duplicates hash-addressing + atomic-write + approval-stamping that storage.ts already provides; more surface, more drift.
Diverges from 'persist follows the established artifact shape' — a bespoke format is explicitly ruled out by the HLD framework summary.
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: A bespoke store/lookup is the exact 'separate place to go looking' ac3 forbids (ac3 violates) and diverges from the storage.ts peer + established-artifact-shape sc1 requires (sc1 violates, k6/k7). Ranked lowest.
